technical language that it often involves. We therefore
produced an [accessible and clear briefing on REDD+](https://globalforestcoalition.org/15-years-of-redd/) for
newcomers in four languages ahead of the UN General
Assembly and Climate Week NYC.

As part of our work to expose the impacts of forest
offsets for aviation we produced two short case studies:
[one focused on offsetting through industrial charcoal
production in Brazil, which was published on](https://globalforestcoalition.org/15-years-of-rhttps://globalforestcoalition.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/vallourec-CORSIA-case-study.pdfedd/)
International Civil Aviation Day, and another on the
Valdivia biomass plant in Chile that is based on research
undertaken in 2020 but will be published in mid-2021.

Another key activity was campaigning with
our European members and allies to
oppose attempts by big oil companies to
base their mitigation efforts on offsets and
other false solutions. We gave a
[presentation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9D9SM3JEqQs) targeting Shell’s false solutions
as part of “Caught in the Net,” a webinar
series organized by our member group
Biofuelwatch. Coinciding with the online Net
Zero Festival, we published an article entitled
[“Roll up, roll up! The Net Zero Circus is coming
to a forest near you” that targeted Net Zero](https://globalforestcoalition.org/net-zero-circus/)
commitments by fossil fuel companies.

We continued our

collaboration with different

Network’s Biomass Working

Group, and we
collaborated in
